_about: Standards the K-12 PBL builder plans projects from. Snapshotted from the standards table, which is itself seeded from scripts/seed-standards-*.ts, so the builder stays reproducible without a database. ELA and Math only: the project holds no Science or Social Studies standards, and those are not invented here.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Partition shapes into halves and quarters
standards.text: Partition circles and rectangles into two and four equal shares, describe the shares using the words halves, fourths, and quarters, and understand that decomposing into more equal shares creates smaller shares.
standards.target: I can split a shape into equal parts and name them halves or quarters.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Order objects by length
standards.text: Order three objects by length, and compare the lengths of two objects indirectly by using a third object.
standards.target: I can put things in order by length, even when I cannot move them.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Understand two-digit place value
standards.text: Understand that the two digits of a two-digit number represent amounts of tens and ones, including that 10 can be thought of as a bundle of ten ones called a ten.
standards.target: I can say how many tens and how many ones are in a number.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Add within 100 using place value
standards.text: Add within 100, including a two-digit number and a one-digit number and a two-digit number and a multiple of ten, using concrete models, drawings and strategies based on place value.
standards.target: I can add a small number or a whole ten to a two-digit number.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Solve addition and subtraction word problems within 20
standards.text: Use addition and subtraction within 20 to solve word problems involving situations of adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart, and comparing.
standards.target: I can work out a word problem by deciding whether to join amounts or take them apart.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Use properties of operations to add
standards.text: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract, including that addition can be done in any order and that three numbers can be grouped in any way.
standards.target: I can add numbers in whatever order makes it easiest.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Understand what the equal sign means
standards.text: Understand the meaning of the equal sign, and determine if equations involving addition and subtraction are true or false.
standards.target: I know the equal sign means both sides are worth the same.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Shapes by attribute, any way up
standards.text: Recognize and draw shapes having specified attributes, such as a given number of angles or a given number of equal faces.
standards.target: I can still name a triangle when it is balanced on a point.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Partition a rectangle into equal squares
standards.text: Partition a rectangle into rows and columns of same-size squares and count to find the total number of them.
standards.target: I can split a rectangle into squares that are all the same size.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Split shapes into halves, thirds and fourths
standards.text: Partition circles and rectangles into two, three, or four equal shares, describe the shares using the words halves, thirds, half of, a third of, and recognize that equal shares of identical wholes need not have the same shape.
standards.target: I can split a shape into equal parts and name them, even if they look different.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Measure length with the right tool
standards.text: Measure the length of an object by selecting and using appropriate tools such as rulers, yardsticks, meter sticks, and measuring tapes.
standards.target: I can pick the right tool and measure how long something is.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Smaller unit, bigger number
standards.text: Measure the length of an object twice, using different length units; describe how the two measurements relate to the size of the unit.
standards.target: I can explain why the same desk is 30 inches and only 2 feet.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Estimate against something you know
standards.text: Estimate lengths using units of inches, feet, centimeters, and meters.
standards.target: I can compare to a paper clip or a door instead of guessing.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: How much longer is a difference
standards.text: Measure to determine how much longer one object is than another, expressing the difference in a standard length unit.
standards.target: I can hear that how much longer means subtract.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Length word problems, with the unit
standards.text: Use addition and subtraction within 100 to solve word problems involving lengths given in the same units.
standards.target: I can solve a length problem and label my answer with the unit.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Jumps on a number line
standards.text: Represent whole numbers as lengths on a number line diagram and represent whole-number sums and differences within 100.
standards.target: I can count the spaces, not the tick marks.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Time to the nearest five minutes
standards.text: Tell and write time from analog and digital clocks to the nearest five minutes, using a.m. and p.m.
standards.target: I can read the hour hand first, then the minutes.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Solve money problems
standards.text: Solve word problems involving dollar bills, quarters, dimes, nickels and pennies, using dollar and cent symbols appropriately.
standards.target: I can work out how much money I have and how much change I get.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Bar graphs, and reading the scale
standards.text: Draw a picture graph and a bar graph to represent a data set with up to four categories; solve problems using information in the graphs.
standards.target: I can check the scale before I read a bar.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Measure, then make a line plot
standards.text: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths of several objects; show the measurements by making a line plot.
standards.target: I can make a line plot where the spacing tells the truth about my data.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Understand three-digit place value
standards.text: Understand that the three digits of a three-digit number represent amounts of hundreds, tens, and ones.
standards.target: I can say what each digit in a three-digit number is worth.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Skip count from anywhere
standards.text: Count within 1000; skip-count by 5s, 10s, and 100s.
standards.target: I can skip count by tens starting at 250, not just at zero.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: One number, three ways
standards.text: Read and write numbers to 1000 using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form.
standards.target: I can write a number as a numeral, in words, and in expanded form.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Compare by place, not by digit
standards.text: Compare two three-digit numbers based on meanings of the hundreds, tens, and ones digits, using >, =, and < symbols.
standards.target: I can compare the hundreds first and say why that comes first.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Add and subtract fluently within 100
standards.text: Fluently add and subtract within 100 using strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and the relationship between addition and subtraction.
standards.target: I can add and subtract two-digit numbers using a strategy that fits.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Add four numbers the easy way round
standards.text: Add up to four two-digit numbers using strategies based on place value and properties of operations.
standards.target: I can look for pairs that make ten before I start adding.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Add and subtract within 1000
standards.text: Add and subtract within 1000, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value.
standards.target: I can tell when I need to regroup and when I do not.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Ten or a hundred more, in your head
standards.text: Mentally add 10 or 100 to, or subtract 10 or 100 from, a given number 100-900.
standards.target: I can say which digit changes and do it without writing anything.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Explain why the strategy works
standards.text: Explain why addition and subtraction strategies work, using place value and the properties of operations.
standards.target: I can say why my way works, not just what I did.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Solve one- and two-step problems within 100
standards.text: Use addition and subtraction within 100 to solve one- and two-step word problems involving situations of adding to, taking from, putting together, taking apart and comparing.
standards.target: I can solve a word problem that needs one step or two.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Add and subtract fluently within 20
standards.text: Fluently add and subtract within 20 using mental strategies. By end of Grade 2, know from memory all sums of two one-digit numbers.
standards.target: I can add and subtract small numbers quickly using a strategy that fits.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Odd and even by pairing
standards.text: Determine whether a group of objects (up to 20) has an odd or even number of members; write an equation to express an even number as a sum of two equal addends.
standards.target: I can pair things up to find out if a group is odd or even, and say why.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Arrays and repeated addition
standards.text: Use addition to find the total number of objects arranged in rectangular arrays with up to 5 rows and 5 columns; write an equation as a sum of equal addends.
standards.target: I can say three rows of four and write 4 + 4 + 4 instead of counting every square.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Sort shapes by what they have in common
standards.text: Understand that shapes in different categories may share attributes, that shared attributes can define a larger category, and recognize rhombuses, rectangles and squares as examples of quadrilaterals.
standards.target: I can group shapes by what they share, not just what they look like.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Equal areas, different shapes
standards.text: Partition shapes into parts with equal areas; express the area of each part as a unit fraction of the whole.
standards.target: I can split a shape into equal areas that do not have to look the same.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Tell time to the minute
standards.text: Tell and write time to the nearest minute and measure time intervals in minutes, solving word problems involving addition and subtraction of time intervals.
standards.target: I can read a clock to the minute and work out how long something took.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Mass is not size
standards.text: Measure and estimate liquid volumes and masses of objects using grams, kilograms, and liters; solve one-step problems involving these units.
standards.target: I can choose the right unit and know a big thing can be light.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Scaled graphs, where a square is not one
standards.text: Draw a scaled picture graph and a scaled bar graph to represent a data set with several categories; solve problems using the graphs.
standards.target: I can read the key before I read a bar.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Measure to the quarter inch
standards.text: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths using rulers marked with halves and fourths of an inch; show the data on a line plot.
standards.target: I can measure to the nearest quarter inch instead of rounding to whole ones.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Area is covering
standards.text: Recognize area as an attribute of plane figures and understand concepts of area measurement.
standards.target: I can say whether a question is about covering or about going around.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Count the squares, all of them
standards.text: Measure areas by counting unit squares.
standards.target: I can count area without skipping or double-counting.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Relate area to multiplication
standards.text: Relate area to the operations of multiplication and addition, including finding area by tiling and by multiplying side lengths.
standards.target: I can find area by covering a shape with squares or by multiplying its sides.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Perimeter goes around
standards.text: Solve real world and mathematical problems involving perimeters of polygons, including finding an unknown side length.
standards.target: I can find a missing side when I know the perimeter.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Round by asking which is closer
standards.text: Use place value understanding to round whole numbers to the nearest 10 or 100.
standards.target: I can put the number on a line and see which benchmark is nearer.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Add and subtract within 1000
standards.text: Fluently add and subtract within 1000 using strategies and algorithms based on place value, properties of operations, and the relationship between addition and subtraction.
standards.target: I can add and subtract three-digit numbers and know when to regroup.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Why the zero appears
standards.text: Multiply one-digit whole numbers by multiples of 10 in the range 10-90 using strategies based on place value.
standards.target: I can explain why 4 × 30 is 120 instead of just adding a zero.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Understand a fraction as parts of a whole
standards.text: Understand a fraction 1/b as the quantity formed by 1 part when a whole is partitioned into b equal parts; understand a fraction a/b as the quantity formed by a parts of size 1/b.
standards.target: I can explain what the top and bottom numbers of a fraction each tell me.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: A fraction is a number on the line
standards.text: Understand a fraction as a number on the number line; represent fractions on a number line diagram.
standards.target: I can find where three quarters lives between zero and one.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Compare fractions and explain equivalence
standards.text: Explain equivalence of fractions in special cases, and compare fractions by reasoning about their size, recognising that comparisons are valid only when the two fractions refer to the same whole.
standards.target: I can tell which fraction is bigger and show why two fractions are the same.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Interpret products of whole numbers
standards.text: Interpret products of whole numbers, e.g., interpret 5 × 7 as the total number of objects in 5 groups of 7 objects each.
standards.target: I can explain what a multiplication expression means using equal groups.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Division has two meanings
standards.text: Interpret whole-number quotients of whole numbers as the number of objects in each share or the number of shares.
standards.target: I can tell whether a problem is asking how many groups or how many in each group.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Model the situation, not the keywords
standards.text: Use multiplication and division within 100 to solve word problems in situations involving equal groups, arrays, and measurement quantities.
standards.target: I can draw what is happening instead of hunting for a keyword.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: The equal sign means balance
standards.text: Determine the unknown whole number in a multiplication or division equation relating three whole numbers.
standards.target: I can solve 8 × ? = 48 because the equal sign means the two sides match.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Break a factor apart
standards.text: Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide.
standards.target: I can turn 7 × 8 into 7 × 5 plus 7 × 3.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Division is a missing factor
standards.text: Understand division as an unknown-factor problem.
standards.target: I can use a multiplication fact I already know to divide.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Facts from anchors, then from memory
standards.text: Fluently multiply and divide within 100. By the end of grade 3, know from memory all products of two one-digit numbers.
standards.target: I can build the hard facts from the ones I already know.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Solve two-step word problems
standards.text: Solve two-step word problems using the four operations. Represent these problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity, and assess the reasonableness of answers.
standards.target: I can solve a problem that needs two steps and check my answer makes sense.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Explain the pattern, not just spot it
standards.text: Identify arithmetic patterns, including patterns in the addition table or multiplication table, and explain them using properties of operations.
standards.target: I can say why the pattern happens, not just that it does.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Draw and identify lines and angles
standards.text: Draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines. Identify these in two-dimensional figures.
standards.target: I can draw and name the different kinds of lines and angles.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Check the attributes one at a time
standards.text: Classify two-dimensional figures based on the presence or absence of parallel or perpendicular lines, or the presence or absence of angles of a specified size.
standards.target: I can classify by testing attributes rather than by how it looks.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Fold it to test the symmetry
standards.text: Recognize a line of symmetry for a two-dimensional figure; identify line-symmetric figures and draw lines of symmetry.
standards.target: I can test a line of symmetry by folding instead of guessing.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Smaller unit, more of them
standards.text: Know relative sizes of measurement units within one system of units; express measurements in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit.
standards.target: I can work out whether to multiply or divide by thinking about the unit.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Convert before you combine
standards.text: Use the four operations to solve word problems involving distances, intervals of time, liquid volumes, masses of objects, and money.
standards.target: I can put everything in one unit before I add it.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Use area and perimeter formulas
standards.text: Apply the area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real world and mathematical problems, including finding an unknown side length from a known area or perimeter.
standards.target: I can find area or perimeter, and work backwards to a missing side.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Line plots in halves, quarters and eighths
standards.text: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit; solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions.
standards.target: I can space fractional intervals evenly so the data tells the truth.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: The opening, not the arms
standards.text: Recognize angles as geometric shapes formed wherever two rays share a common endpoint, and understand concepts of angle measurement.
standards.target: I know a longer ray does not make a bigger angle.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Which scale on the protractor
standards.text: Measure angles in whole-number degrees using a protractor; sketch angles of specified measure.
standards.target: I can estimate acute or obtuse first so I pick the right scale.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Angles add, when they are adjacent
standards.text: Recognize angle measure as additive; solve addition and subtraction problems to find unknown angles on a diagram.
standards.target: I can find a missing angle and check the parts actually touch.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Ten times the place to its right
standards.text: Recognize that in a multi-digit whole number, a digit in one place represents ten times what it represents in the place to its right.
standards.target: I can explain why 700 is ten times 70, not just say the rule.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Large numbers, three ways, no and
standards.text: Read and write multi-digit whole numbers using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form; compare two numbers using >, =, and <.
standards.target: I can write a big number in words without putting and in it.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Round the target place only
standards.text: Use place value understanding to round multi-digit whole numbers to any place.
standards.target: I can round once, to the place asked for, and stop.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Estimate first, then subtract across zeros
standards.text: Fluently add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.
standards.target: I can estimate first so I notice when my answer is wrong.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Multiply multi-digit whole numbers
standards.text: Multiply a whole number of up to four digits by a one-digit whole number, and multiply two two-digit numbers, using strategies based on place value and the properties of operations.
standards.target: I can multiply bigger numbers by breaking them apart by place value.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Divide with remainders
standards.text: Find whole-number quotients and remainders with up to four-digit dividends and one-digit divisors, using strategies based on place value and the properties of operations.
standards.target: I can divide a big number by a small one and explain each step.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: More pieces, same amount
standards.text: Explain why a fraction a/b is equivalent to a fraction (n x a)/(n x b) using visual fraction models.
standards.target: I can show why cutting into more pieces does not make more.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Compare fractions, not their digits
standards.text: Compare two fractions with different numerators and different denominators; record the results with the symbols >, =, or <.
standards.target: I can use a half as a benchmark instead of comparing the numbers separately.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Add and subtract fractions with like denominators
standards.text: Understand a fraction a/b with a > 1 as a sum of fractions 1/b, and add and subtract fractions with like denominators, including mixed numbers.
standards.target: I can add and subtract fractions that share a denominator by counting the parts.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: A fraction times a whole number
standards.text: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction by a whole number.
standards.target: I can see three lots of one quarter as three quarters.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Tenths into hundredths first
standards.text: Express a fraction with denominator 10 as an equivalent fraction with denominator 100, and use this to add two fractions with these denominators.
standards.target: I can rewrite tenths as hundredths before adding.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Write fractions as decimals
standards.text: Use decimal notation for fractions with denominators 10 or 100, and locate these decimals on a number line.
standards.target: I can write tenths and hundredths as decimals and find them on a number line.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: 0.5 is bigger than 0.45
standards.text: Compare two decimals to hundredths by reasoning about their size; record the results with the symbols >, =, or <.
standards.target: I can compare decimals by place value, not by how many digits there are.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Times as many is not more than
standards.text: Interpret a multiplication equation as a comparison; represent verbal statements of multiplicative comparisons as multiplication equations.
standards.target: I can tell four times as many from four more than.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Is it adding or multiplying
standards.text: Multiply or divide to solve word problems involving multiplicative comparison, distinguishing multiplicative from additive comparison.
standards.target: I can work out the relationship before picking an operation.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Solve multistep problems and read the remainder
standards.text: Solve multistep word problems posed with whole numbers using the four operations, including problems in which remainders must be interpreted, and assess the reasonableness of answers.
standards.target: I can solve a several-step problem and know what to do with a remainder.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Every factor pair, and prime or not
standards.text: Find all factor pairs for a whole number in the range 1-100; determine whether a given whole number is prime or composite.
standards.target: I can know when I have found every factor, and I know one is neither.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Say the rule, not just the next term
standards.text: Generate a number or shape pattern that follows a given rule; identify apparent features of the pattern that were not explicit in the rule.
standards.target: I can state the rule so I could run the pattern backwards.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Plot points on the coordinate plane
standards.text: Use a pair of perpendicular number lines, called axes, to define a coordinate system, and understand that the first number indicates how far to travel from the origin along the first axis and the second number how far along the second.
standards.target: I can plot a point using its two numbers, in the right order.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Find the volume of a rectangular prism
standards.text: Relate volume to the operations of multiplication and addition and solve real world and mathematical problems involving volume of right rectangular prisms.
standards.target: I can find how much space a box holds and explain why the formula works.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Understand place value across the decimal point
standards.text: Recognize that in a multi-digit number, a digit in one place represents 10 times as much as it represents in the place to its right and 1/10 of what it represents in the place to its left.
standards.target: I can explain how each place is ten times the one beside it, both ways.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Compute with decimals to hundredths
standards.text: Add, subtract, multiply and divide decimals to hundredths, using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value, and relate the strategy to a written method.
standards.target: I can add, subtract, multiply and divide decimals and explain why it works.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators
standards.text: Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators (including mixed numbers) by replacing given fractions with equivalent fractions to produce a like denominator.
standards.target: I can rename fractions so they share a denominator, then add or subtract them.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Multiply a fraction by a fraction
standards.text: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction or whole number by a fraction, including finding the area of a rectangle with fractional side lengths.
standards.target: I can multiply fractions and explain why the answer gets smaller.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Use brackets and evaluate in order
standards.text: Use parentheses, brackets or braces in numerical expressions, and evaluate expressions with these symbols.
standards.target: I can work out an expression in the right order, brackets first.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Write, read and evaluate expressions with variables
standards.text: Write, read, and evaluate expressions in which letters stand for numbers, including translating between words and algebraic expressions and evaluating at specific values.
standards.target: I can turn words into an expression with a letter and work out its value.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Solve one-step equations
standards.text: Solve real-world and mathematical problems by writing and solving equations of the form x + p = q and px = q for cases in which p, q and x are all non-negative rational numbers.
standards.target: I can write an equation for a problem and solve it.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Find area by composing and decomposing
standards.text: Find the area of right triangles, other triangles, special quadrilaterals, and polygons by composing into rectangles or decomposing into triangles, and apply these techniques to real-world problems.
standards.target: I can find the area of an awkward shape by cutting it into easy ones.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Divide a fraction by a fraction
standards.text: Interpret and compute quotients of fractions, and solve word problems involving division of fractions by fractions, using visual fraction models and equations.
standards.target: I can work out how many of one fraction fit inside another, and say why.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Place rational numbers on a number line
standards.text: Understand a rational number as a point on the number line, extending number line diagrams and coordinate axes to represent points with negative coordinates.
standards.target: I can put positive and negative numbers in the right place on a number line.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Understand what a ratio is
standards.text: Understand the concept of a ratio and use ratio language to describe a ratio relationship between two quantities.
standards.target: I can describe a relationship between two amounts using ratio language.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Use ratio reasoning to solve problems
standards.text: Use ratio and rate reasoning to solve real-world and mathematical problems, e.g., by reasoning about tables of equivalent ratios, tape diagrams, double number line diagrams, or equations.
standards.target: I can solve ratio problems using a table, a diagram, or an equation.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Summarize a data set
standards.text: Summarize numerical data sets in relation to their context, reporting the number of observations, describing the attribute measured, and giving measures of center and variability.
standards.target: I can describe a set of data with a typical value and how spread out it is.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Add, factor and expand linear expressions
standards.text: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add, subtract, factor, and expand linear expressions with rational coefficients.
standards.target: I can rewrite an expression in a different but equal form.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Solve equations and inequalities from real problems
standards.text: Use variables to represent quantities in a real-world or mathematical problem, and construct simple equations and inequalities to solve problems by reasoning about the quantities.
standards.target: I can turn a word problem into an equation and solve it.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Solve area, volume and surface area problems
standards.text: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, volume and surface area of two- and three-dimensional objects composed of triangles, quadrilaterals, polygons, cubes, and right prisms.
standards.target: I can work out area, surface area or volume and know which one the question wants.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Add and subtract rational numbers
standards.text: Apply and extend previous understandings of addition and subtraction to add and subtract rational numbers, representing addition and subtraction on a horizontal or vertical number line diagram.
standards.target: I can add and subtract positive and negative numbers and show it on a number line.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Multiply and divide rational numbers
standards.text: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division and of fractions to multiply and divide rational numbers, including understanding the rules for signs.
standards.target: I can multiply and divide positive and negative numbers and explain the sign.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Recognize and represent proportional relationships
standards.text: Recognize and represent proportional relationships between quantities, identifying the constant of proportionality in tables, graphs, equations, diagrams, and verbal descriptions.
standards.target: I can tell whether a relationship is proportional and find its constant.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Solve percent and ratio problems
standards.text: Use proportional relationships to solve multistep ratio and percent problems, including simple interest, tax, markups, discounts, tips, and percent increase and decrease.
standards.target: I can work out discounts, tips and percent changes.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Use a sample to learn about a population
standards.text: Understand that statistics can be used to gain information about a population by examining a sample, and that generalizations are valid only if the sample is representative.
standards.target: I can tell whether a sample is fair enough to say something about everyone.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Understand the probability of a chance event
standards.text: Understand that the probability of a chance event is a number between 0 and 1 that expresses the likelihood of the event occurring, with larger numbers indicating greater likelihood.
standards.target: I can put the chance of something happening on a scale from 0 to 1.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Apply the laws of exponents
standards.text: Know and apply the properties of integer exponents to generate equivalent numerical expressions, including products, quotients, powers of powers, and negative exponents.
standards.target: I can simplify expressions with exponents and explain the rule I used.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Graph proportional relationships and read slope
standards.text: Graph proportional relationships, interpreting the unit rate as the slope of the graph, and compare two different proportional relationships represented in different ways.
standards.target: I can graph a proportional relationship and say what its steepness means.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Solve linear equations in one variable
standards.text: Solve linear equations in one variable, including equations with rational number coefficients and equations whose solutions require expanding expressions using the distributive property and collecting like terms.
standards.target: I can solve a linear equation and say whether it has one, none, or infinite solutions.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Understand what makes a relationship a function
standards.text: Understand that a function is a rule that assigns to each input exactly one output; the graph of a function is the set of ordered pairs consisting of an input and the corresponding output.
standards.target: I can tell whether a relationship is a function and say why.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Build a function from a situation
standards.text: Construct a function to model a linear relationship between two quantities, determining the rate of change and initial value from a description, a table, or two points.
standards.target: I can write the rule for a situation and say what the numbers mean.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Discover what transformations preserve
standards.text: Verify experimentally the properties of rotations, reflections and translations, including that lines are taken to lines, and that lengths and angle measures are preserved.
standards.target: I can slide, flip and turn a shape and say what stays the same.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem
standards.text: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to determine unknown side lengths in right triangles in real-world and mathematical problems in two and three dimensions.
standards.target: I can find a missing side of a right triangle and know when the theorem applies.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Find the volume of curved solids
standards.text: Know the formulas for the volumes of cones, cylinders and spheres and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems.
standards.target: I can find the volume of a cylinder, cone or sphere and know which formula fits.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Tell rational numbers from irrational ones
standards.text: Know that numbers that are not rational are called irrational, and understand informally that every number has a decimal expansion — repeating or terminating for rational numbers.
standards.target: I can tell whether a number can be written as a fraction, and say how I know.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Read a scatter plot for association
standards.text: Construct and interpret scatter plots for bivariate measurement data to investigate patterns of association between two quantities, describing clustering, outliers, and the form and direction of any association.
standards.target: I can plot two measurements together and describe how they relate.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Create equations from a situation
standards.text: Create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them to solve problems, including equations arising from linear and quadratic functions and simple rational and exponential functions.
standards.target: I can turn a real situation into an equation and solve it.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Solve quadratic equations
standards.text: Solve quadratic equations in one variable by inspection, taking square roots, completing the square, factoring and the quadratic formula, recognizing when a solution is not real.
standards.target: I can pick the quickest way to solve a quadratic rather than always using the formula.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Read the structure of an expression
standards.text: Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context, identifying the parts of an expression and interpreting complicated expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity.
standards.target: I can look at an expression and say what each part is doing.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Build a function to model a situation
standards.text: Write a function that describes a relationship between two quantities, determining an explicit expression or a recursive process from a context.
standards.target: I can build the rule for a situation, not just use one I was given.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Read the key features of a graph
standards.text: For a function that models a relationship between two quantities, interpret key features of graphs and tables in terms of the quantities, including intercepts, intervals of increase and decrease, maxima and minima, and end behavior.
standards.target: I can describe what a graph is telling me about the real situation behind it.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Tell linear growth from exponential
standards.text: Construct linear and exponential functions, including arithmetic and geometric sequences, given a graph, a description of a relationship, or two input-output pairs.
standards.target: I can tell whether something grows by adding or by multiplying, and write the rule.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Solve right triangles with trigonometry
standards.text: Use trigonometric ratios and the Pythagorean Theorem to solve right triangles in applied problems.
standards.target: I can find a missing side or angle in a right triangle and know which ratio to use.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Count to 100 by ones and by tens
standards.text: Count to 100 by ones and by tens.
standards.target: I can count all the way to 100, one at a time and ten at a time.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Connect counting to how many
standards.text: Understand the relationship between numbers and quantities; connect counting to cardinality, including that the last number said tells the number of objects counted.
standards.target: I know the last number I say is how many there are.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Name shapes however they are turned
standards.text: Correctly name shapes regardless of their orientations or overall size.
standards.target: I know a triangle is still a triangle even when it is turned or tiny.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Compare two things directly
standards.text: Directly compare two objects with a measurable attribute in common, to see which object has more of or less of the attribute, and describe the difference.
standards.target: I can line two things up and say which is longer or heavier.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: See teen numbers as ten and some more
standards.text: Compose and decompose numbers from 11 to 19 into ten ones and some further ones, and record each composition or decomposition by a drawing or equation.
standards.target: I know 14 is one ten and four more.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Represent addition and subtraction
standards.text: Represent addition and subtraction with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds, acting out situations, verbal explanations, expressions, or equations.
standards.target: I can show adding and taking away with objects, drawings, or numbers.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Break a number into two parts
standards.text: Decompose numbers less than or equal to 10 into pairs in more than one way, and record each decomposition by a drawing or equation.
standards.target: I can split a number into two parts in more than one way.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Work out what a new word means
standards.text: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 1 reading and content, choosing flexibly from an array of strategies including sentence-level context and common affixes.
standards.target: I can use the rest of the sentence to work out a word I do not know.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Use standard English grammar when writing and speaking
standards.text: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking, including collective nouns, irregular plurals, and past tense of irregular verbs.
standards.target: I can use the right words and word endings when I write and talk.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Capitals, commas and apostrophes
standards.text: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing, including apostrophes for contractions and possessives.
standards.target: I can use an apostrophe only when something is missing or owned.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Talk one way to a friend, another to a principal
standards.text: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening, comparing formal and informal uses of English.
standards.target: I can choose my words to suit who I am talking to.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Work out new words in grade 2 texts
standards.text: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 2 reading and content, using sentence context, known prefixes, compound words and glossaries.
standards.target: I can use clues in the sentence and the parts of a word to work out what it means.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Words that nearly mean the same thing
standards.text: Demonstrate understanding of word relationships and nuances in word meanings, including shades of meaning among closely related verbs and adjectives.
standards.target: I can put words in order from gentle to strong.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Use the new word, do not just know it
standards.text: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, reading and being read to, and responding to texts, including adjectives and adverbs to describe.
standards.target: I can put a new word into my own writing and talking.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Explain what each kind of word does
standards.text: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage, including explaining the function of nouns, pronouns, verbs, adjectives and adverbs in particular sentences.
standards.target: I can name the job a word is doing in a sentence.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Punctuating what someone said
standards.text: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing, including commas in dialogue and possessives.
standards.target: I can punctuate dialogue with the comma and the marks in the right places.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Choosing words for effect
standards.text: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening, choosing words and phrases for effect.
standards.target: I can tell when writing needs to sound different from talking.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Work out what unfamiliar words mean
standards.text: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 3 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.
standards.target: I can figure out a new word using the sentence around it and its word parts.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Knew, believed, suspected
standards.text: Demonstrate understanding of word relationships and nuances in word meanings, including shades of meaning among related words.
standards.target: I can order words by how certain they are.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Academic words in your own mouth
standards.text: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate conversational, general academic, and domain-specific words and phrases.
standards.target: I can use an academic word outside the lesson it came from.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Use grade 4 grammar correctly
standards.text: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking, including relative pronouns, progressive verb tenses, modal auxiliaries, and prepositional phrases.
standards.target: I can use tenses, pronouns and phrases correctly in my own writing.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: The comma before and, when it earns it
standards.text: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing, including commas in compound sentences and quotations.
standards.target: I can tell when the comma before and is needed and when it is not.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Precise beats impressive
standards.text: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening, choosing words and phrases to convey ideas precisely.
standards.target: I can pick the exact word rather than the longest one.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Greek and Latin roots, then verify
standards.text: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 4 reading and content.
standards.target: I can use roots to get a meaning, then check it fits.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Similes, metaphors and idioms
standards.text: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.
standards.target: I can explain what a figure of speech actually means.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Words that survive the test
standards.text: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases.
standards.target: I can use an academic word in my own writing weeks later.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Determine word meanings and use context clues
standards.text: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 5 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.
standards.target: I can use context clues and strategies to figure out what unfamiliar words mean.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Understand figurative language and word nuance
standards.text: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings, including similes, metaphors, and idioms.
standards.target: I can tell when words mean something other than exactly what they say.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Work out unfamiliar words in grade 6 texts
standards.text: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 6 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies including context, Greek and Latin affixes, and reference materials.
standards.target: I can use context, word parts and a dictionary to pin down a word's meaning.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Work out unfamiliar words in grade 7 texts
standards.text: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 7 reading and content, using context, word parts and reference materials, and verifying the inferred meaning.
standards.target: I can work out a word from clues and then check whether I was right.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Work out demanding vocabulary
standards.text: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grades 9-10 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies and verifying the inferred meaning.
standards.target: I can work out a difficult word from context and word parts, then check I was right.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Rewrite expressions with rational exponents
standards.text: Rewrite expressions involving radicals and rational exponents using the properties of exponents.
standards.target: I can move between a root and a fractional exponent, whichever is easier to work with.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Blend and segment the sounds in spoken words
standards.text: Demonstrate understanding of spoken words, syllables, and sounds (phonemes), including blending and segmenting single-syllable words.
standards.target: I can break words into sounds and push the sounds back together.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Use grade 1 phonics to read words
standards.text: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words, including consonant digraphs, final -e and common vowel teams, and counting syllables to decode longer words.
standards.target: I can use letter patterns to read longer words on my own.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Use phonics to decode words
standards.text: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words, including long and short vowels, vowel teams, and common prefixes and suffixes.
standards.target: I can use what I know about letters and sounds to read new words.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Long and short vowels in one-syllable words
standards.text: Distinguish long and short vowels when reading regularly spelled one-syllable words.
standards.target: I can tell if a vowel is long or short by looking at the whole word.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Vowel teams make one sound
standards.text: Know spelling-sound correspondences for additional common vowel teams.
standards.target: I can read two vowels together as one sound.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Split a two-syllable word and read it
standards.text: Decode regularly spelled two-syllable words with long vowels.
standards.target: I can break a long word into syllables and try again if my first split is wrong.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Prefixes and suffixes on a base word
standards.text: Decode words with common prefixes and suffixes.
standards.target: I can find the base word underneath and use the word part to help me.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Words that break the rules
standards.text: Identify words with inconsistent but common spelling-sound correspondences.
standards.target: I can spot the tricky part of a word that does not follow the rule.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Sight words, instantly and in sentences
standards.text: Recognize and read grade-appropriate irregularly spelled words.
standards.target: I know my sight words in a real book, not just on a card.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Read grade 2 text smoothly
standards.text: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension, reading on-level text with purpose and understanding and with appropriate rate and expression.
standards.target: I can read smoothly enough to still know what the story means.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Know why you are reading before you start
standards.text: Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.
standards.target: I can say what I am reading for before I begin.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Read aloud smoothly, with expression
standards.text: Read grade-level text orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.
standards.target: I can read out loud so it sounds like talking, not racing.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Notice a mistake and fix it yourself
standards.text: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.
standards.target: I can hear when it stopped making sense and go back.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: What the prefix actually means
standards.text: Identify and know the meaning of the most common prefixes and derivational suffixes.
standards.target: I can use the word part to work out what the word means.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Latin suffixes as one chunk
standards.text: Decode words with common Latin suffixes.
standards.target: I can read -tion as one piece instead of sounding out every letter.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Read the whole long word
standards.text: Decode multisyllable words.
standards.target: I can decode all the way through instead of guessing from the start.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Irregular words, read quickly
standards.text: Read grade-appropriate irregularly spelled words.
standards.target: I can read island and answer without sounding out the silent bit.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Read accurately and fluently to understand
standards.text: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension, including reading on-level text with purpose, appropriate rate, expression, and self-correction.
standards.target: I can read smoothly enough that I still understand what I read.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Read differently depending on why
standards.text: Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.
standards.target: I can skim for a fact or read closely, depending on what I need.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Accuracy and expression, not just speed
standards.text: Read grade-level prose and poetry orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.
standards.target: I can read so a listener hears the meaning, not just the words.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Fix it when the meaning breaks, not just the word
standards.text: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.
standards.target: I can notice when a sentence I read correctly still made no sense.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Decode it and know what it means
standards.text: Use combined knowledge of all letter-sound correspondences, syllabication patterns, and morphology to read accurately unfamiliar multisyllabic words.
standards.target: I can read a long word and then say what it means.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Read grade 4 text smoothly and accurately
standards.text: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension, reading grade-level prose and poetry orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.
standards.target: I can read longer texts smoothly enough that the meaning still comes through.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Purpose changes the reading
standards.text: Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.
standards.target: I can read the same page differently depending on why.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Phrases, not words one at a time
standards.text: Read grade-level prose and poetry orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.
standards.target: I can group words into phrases so long sentences hold together.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Did the whole passage make sense
standards.text: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.
standards.target: I can check the paragraph made sense, not just the words in it.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Long words, in and out of context
standards.text: Use combined knowledge of all letter-sound correspondences, syllabication patterns, and morphology to read accurately unfamiliar multisyllabic words in context and out of context.
standards.target: I can read an unfamiliar long word and say what its parts mean.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Read for the reason you are reading
standards.text: Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.
standards.target: I can match how I read to why I am reading.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Read aloud so the meaning carries
standards.text: Read grade-level prose and poetry orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.
standards.target: I can read a long sentence in phrases so a listener follows it.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Catch the breakdown, repair it
standards.text: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.
standards.target: I can notice a paragraph that made no sense and go back far enough.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Understand how print works
standards.text: Demonstrate understanding of the organization and basic features of print, including directionality, word boundaries, and letter recognition.
standards.target: I can show which way the words go and where one word stops and the next begins.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Hear the sounds inside spoken words
standards.text: Demonstrate understanding of spoken words, syllables, and sounds, including recognising rhyme, counting syllables, and isolating the initial sound in a word.
standards.target: I can hear rhymes, clap the beats in a word, and say its first sound.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Match letters to the sounds they make
standards.text: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words, including letter-sound correspondences for consonants and the five major vowels, and reading common high-frequency words by sight.
standards.target: I know the sound each letter makes, and I can read some words straight away.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Ask and answer questions about a true text
standards.text: Ask and answer questions about key details in a text.
standards.target: I can ask and answer questions about a book that tells me true things.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Use headings and contents to find things
standards.text: Know and use various text features, including headings, tables of contents, glossaries, electronic menus and icons, to locate key facts or information in a text.
standards.target: I can use the contents page and headings to find what I need.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Analyze rhetoric and point of view
standards.text: Determine an author's point of view or purpose in a text in which the rhetoric is particularly effective, analyzing how style and content contribute to the power, persuasiveness or beauty of the text.
standards.target: I can explain how a piece of writing persuades, not just what it says.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Ask and answer questions about a nonfiction text
standards.text: Ask and answer such questions as who, what, where, when, why, and how to demonstrate understanding of key details in a text.
standards.target: I can ask and answer all six kinds of question about a true text.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Read grade-level nonfiction without giving up
standards.text: By the end of year, read and comprehend informational texts in the grades 2-3 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed.
standards.target: I can read nonfiction at my level and keep going when the words are hard.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Main topic of the text, focus of each paragraph
standards.text: Identify the main topic of a multiparagraph text as well as the focus of specific paragraphs within the text.
standards.target: I can say what the whole text is about and what one paragraph is about.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Connect the events, ideas or steps
standards.text: Describe the connection between a series of historical events, scientific ideas or concepts, or steps in technical procedures in a text.
standards.target: I can show how one step or event leads to the next.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Work out what a topic word means
standards.text: Determine the meaning of words and phrases in a text relevant to a grade 2 topic or subject area.
standards.target: I can figure out a new word using the sentence, the bold print or the glossary.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Use text features to find information
standards.text: Know and use various text features (captions, bold print, subheadings, glossaries, indexes, electronic menus, icons) to locate key facts or information in a text efficiently.
standards.target: I can use headings, bold words, and captions to find what I need fast.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Say why the author wrote it
standards.text: Identify the main purpose of a text, including what the author wants to answer, explain, or describe.
standards.target: I can tell why the author wrote this, not just what it is about.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Explain what the diagram adds
standards.text: Explain how specific images contribute to and clarify a text.
standards.target: I can say what a picture or diagram explains that the words do not.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Find the reason behind the point
standards.text: Describe how reasons support specific points the author makes in a text.
standards.target: I can find what the author wants me to believe and the reason they gave.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Compare two texts on one topic
standards.text: Compare and contrast the most important points presented by two texts on the same topic.
standards.target: I can say what two books on the same topic each told me.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Answer from the text, not from what you knew
standards.text: Ask and answer questions to demonstrate understanding of a text, referring explicitly to the text as the basis for the answers.
standards.target: I can separate what the text said from what I already thought.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Nonfiction, independently, at the top of the band
standards.text: By the end of the year, read and comprehend informational texts at the high end of the grades 2-3 text complexity band independently and proficiently.
standards.target: I can choose nonfiction in independent reading and stay with it.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Find the main idea and the details that support it
standards.text: Determine the main idea of a text; recount the key details and explain how they support the main idea.
standards.target: I can name the big idea of a text and show which details hold it up.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: The chain, not the list
standards.text: Describe the relationship between a series of historical events, scientific ideas, or steps in technical procedures, using time and cause language.
standards.target: I can show how each step caused the next, not just what order they came in.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Subject words that already meant something else
standards.text: Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases in a text relevant to a grade 3 topic or subject area.
standards.target: I can spot when a familiar word is being used in a subject way.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Find it fast with the right tool
standards.text: Use text features and search tools to locate information relevant to a given topic efficiently.
standards.target: I can search with key words instead of a whole sentence.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: The author has a view too
standards.text: Distinguish their own point of view from that of the author of a text.
standards.target: I can find what the author thinks, even when it looks like plain fact.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: A diagram is information, not decoration
standards.text: Use information gained from illustrations and the words in a text to demonstrate understanding of the text.
standards.target: I can read a diagram the way I read a paragraph.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: How one paragraph leads to the next
standards.text: Describe the logical connection between particular sentences and paragraphs in a text.
standards.target: I can name what joins two paragraphs — comparison, cause, or order.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Put the two texts side by side
standards.text: Compare and contrast the most important points and key details presented in two texts on the same topic.
standards.target: I can say where two texts agree and where they part company.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: The sentence, not the paragraph
standards.text: Refer to details and examples in a text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.
standards.target: I can point to the exact sentence that supports my point.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Chunk it rather than skim it
standards.text: By the end of year, read and comprehend informational texts in the grades 4-5 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end.
standards.target: I can break a dense text into sections and summarize as I go.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Determine main idea and supporting details
standards.text: Determine the main idea of a text and explain how it is supported by key details; summarize the text.
standards.target: I can find the main idea of an informational text and explain how details support it.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Explain what happened and why
standards.text: Explain events, procedures, ideas, or concepts in a historical, scientific, or technical text, including what happened and why, based on specific information in the text.
standards.target: I can explain not just what happened but why, using the text.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Current, solution, contract
standards.text: Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words or phrases in a text relevant to a grade 4 topic or subject area.
standards.target: I can spot when a word I know is being used technically.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Describe the structure of a text
standards.text: Describe the overall structure (chronology, comparison, cause/effect, problem/solution) of events, ideas, concepts, or information in a text or part of a text.
standards.target: I can name how a text is organized and show what gave it away.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Firsthand is not automatically right
standards.text: Compare and contrast a firsthand and secondhand account of the same event or topic; describe the differences in focus and information provided.
standards.target: I can say what each kind of account is good at and what it misses.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: What the graph does for the argument
standards.text: Interpret information presented visually, orally, or quantitatively and explain how the information contributes to an understanding of the text.
standards.target: I can say what a chart means for the point the author is making.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Saying it is not proving it
standards.text: Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text.
standards.target: I can tell the difference between a claim and the evidence for it.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Weave the sources, do not stack them
standards.text: Integrate information from two texts on the same topic in order to write or speak about the subject knowledgeably.
standards.target: I can write one account from two sources rather than two summaries.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Quote accurately, and mark the inference
standards.text: Quote accurately from a text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.
standards.target: I can quote the exact words and say which part was my own inference.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Grade-level nonfiction, on your own
standards.text: By the end of the year, read and comprehend informational texts at the high end of the grades 4-5 text complexity band independently and proficiently.
standards.target: I can work through dense nonfiction without giving up on it.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Determine two or more main ideas and summarize
standards.text: Determine two or more main ideas of a text and explain how they are supported by key details; summarize the text.
standards.target: I can find more than one big idea in a text and sum it up without retelling everything.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: How two ideas act on each other
standards.text: Explain the relationships or interactions between two or more individuals, events, ideas, or concepts in a historical, scientific, or technical text based on specific information in the text.
standards.target: I can explain how two things in the text affected each other.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Subject vocabulary in grade 5 texts
standards.text: Determine the meaning of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases in a text relevant to a grade 5 topic or subject area.
standards.target: I can work out a subject word and check the meaning fits.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Compare how two texts are organized
standards.text: Compare and contrast the overall structure of events, ideas, concepts or information in two or more texts.
standards.target: I can say how two texts on the same topic are put together differently.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Several accounts of one event
standards.text: Analyze multiple accounts of the same event or topic, noting important similarities and differences in the point of view they represent.
standards.target: I can say what each account emphasizes and why that differs.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Find the answer fast, across sources
standards.text: Draw on information from multiple print or digital sources, demonstrating the ability to locate an answer to a question quickly or to solve a problem efficiently.
standards.target: I can search several sources and find the answer without reading everything.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Which reason supports which point
standards.text: Explain how an author uses reasons and evidence to support particular points in a text, identifying which reasons and evidence support which point(s).
standards.target: I can match each piece of evidence to the point it actually supports.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Several texts, one account
standards.text: Integrate information from several texts on the same topic in order to write or speak about the subject knowledgeably.
standards.target: I can write one account from three sources rather than three summaries.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Cite evidence in informational text
standards.text: Cite textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.
standards.target: I can back up my analysis of a nonfiction text with the author's own words.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Analyze how a part fits the whole text
standards.text: Analyze how a particular sentence, paragraph, chapter, or section fits into the overall structure of a text and contributes to the development of the ideas.
standards.target: I can explain what a paragraph is doing for the text as a whole.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Trace and evaluate an argument
standards.text: Trace and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, distinguishing claims that are supported by reasons and evidence from claims that are not.
standards.target: I can follow an author's argument and tell which claims are actually backed up.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Determine central ideas and how they develop
standards.text: Determine two or more central ideas in a text and analyze their development over the course of the text; provide an objective summary of the text.
standards.target: I can find more than one central idea and trace how each is built up.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Determine an author's point of view
standards.text: Determine an author's point of view or purpose in a text and analyze how the author distinguishes his or her position from that of others.
standards.target: I can work out what the author thinks and how they set it apart from other views.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Cite evidence that most strongly supports an analysis
standards.text: Cite the textual evidence that most strongly supports an analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.
standards.target: I can pick the strongest evidence for my point, not just any evidence that fits.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Trace a central idea and its supporting ideas
standards.text: Determine a central idea of a text and analyze its development over the course of the text, including its relationship to supporting ideas, and provide an objective summary.
standards.target: I can follow a central idea through a text and show what holds it up.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Analyze the structure of a paragraph
standards.text: Analyze in detail the structure of a specific paragraph in a text, including the role of particular sentences in developing and refining a key concept.
standards.target: I can explain what each sentence in a paragraph is doing for the idea.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Analyze how ideas are built across a text
standards.text: Analyze in detail how an author's ideas or claims are developed and refined by particular sentences, paragraphs, or larger portions of a text.
standards.target: I can explain what a particular passage does for the argument around it.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Ask and answer questions about a true book
standards.text: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about key details in a text.
standards.target: I can ask and answer questions about a book that tells me real things.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Describe characters, settings, and major events
standards.text: Describe characters, settings, and major events in a story, using key details.
standards.target: I can tell who is in the story, where it happens, and what happens, using details.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Analyze an author's choices about structure
standards.text: Analyze the impact of an author's choices regarding how to develop and relate elements of a story or drama, including where a story is set, how the action is ordered, and how the characters are introduced and developed.
standards.target: I can explain why the author told it in this order rather than another.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Ask and answer questions about key details
standards.text: Ask and answer such questions as who, what, where, when, why, and how to demonstrate understanding of key details in a text.
standards.target: I can ask and answer questions about who, what, where, when, why, and how in stories.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Read grade-level stories and notice when you are lost
