standards.text: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature in the grades 2-3 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.
standards.target: I can read stories at my level and stop when they stop making sense.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Recount a story and name its lesson
standards.text: Recount stories, including fables and folktales from diverse cultures, and determine their central message, lesson, or moral.
standards.target: I can retell a story in order and then say what it was teaching me.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Describe how characters respond
standards.text: Describe how characters in a story respond to major events and challenges.
standards.target: I can name a character's problem and describe how they answered it.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Hear how words make rhythm and meaning
standards.text: Describe how words and phrases supply rhythm and meaning in a story, poem, or song.
standards.target: I can find the words that make a poem sound good and say what they add.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Describe how a story is put together
standards.text: Describe the overall structure of a story, including describing how the beginning introduces the story and the ending concludes the action.
standards.target: I can explain what the beginning sets up and how the ending finishes it.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Tell who is speaking, and sound like them
standards.text: Acknowledge differences in the points of view of characters, including by speaking in a different voice for each character when reading dialogue aloud.
standards.target: I can tell who is talking and read them in their own voice.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Read the pictures as well as the words
standards.text: Use information gained from the illustrations and words in a print or digital text to demonstrate understanding of its characters, setting, or plot.
standards.target: I can find things in the picture that the words never told me.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Compare two versions of one story
standards.text: Compare and contrast two or more versions of the same story by different authors or from different cultures.
standards.target: I can say what stayed the same and what changed between two tellings.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Ask and answer questions, referring explicitly to the text
standards.text: Ask and answer questions to demonstrate understanding of a text, referring explicitly to the text as the basis for the answers.
standards.target: I can answer questions about a story and point to the words that prove it.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Read at the top of the band, on your own
standards.text: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature at the high end of the grades 2-3 text complexity band independently and proficiently.
standards.target: I can choose a book that stretches me and finish it.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Find the lesson in a story
standards.text: Recount stories, including fables, folktales and myths from diverse cultures, determine the central message, lesson or moral, and explain how it is conveyed through key details in the text.
standards.target: I can retell a story and say what it teaches, using details that show it.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: How a character's actions drive the plot
standards.text: Describe characters in a story and explain how their actions contribute to the sequence of events.
standards.target: I can describe what a character is like and show how that changed the story.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: When words are not meant literally
standards.text: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, distinguishing literal from nonliteral language.
standards.target: I can tell when a phrase means something other than what it says.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Chapter, scene, stanza
standards.text: Refer to parts of stories, dramas, and poems when writing or speaking about a text, using terms such as chapter, scene, and stanza.
standards.target: I can use the right word for the part of the text I am talking about.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Whose eyes are we seeing through
standards.text: Distinguish their own point of view from that of the narrator or those of the characters.
standards.target: I can say what the narrator thinks and how that differs from what I think.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: What the illustration adds
standards.text: Explain how specific aspects of a text's illustrations contribute to what is conveyed by the words in a story.
standards.target: I can say what a picture adds beyond showing what happened.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Two books, one author, one character
standards.text: Compare and contrast the themes, settings, and plots of stories written by the same author about the same or similar characters.
standards.target: I can compare two books on one thing at a time instead of retelling both.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Refer to details and examples when explaining a text
standards.text: Refer to details and examples in a text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.
standards.target: I can explain what a text says and back it up with details, including things it only hints at.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Finishing is not understanding
standards.text: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature in the grades 4-5 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end.
standards.target: I can check I understood rather than just reaching the last page.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Determine a theme from details in the text
standards.text: Determine a theme of a story, drama, or poem from details in the text; summarize the text.
standards.target: I can work out the message of a story using details, and sum the story up.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Describe a character in depth
standards.text: Describe in depth a character, setting, or event in a story or drama, drawing on specific details in the text such as a character's thoughts, words, or actions.
standards.target: I can describe a character properly using what they think, say and do.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Words that point at a myth
standards.text: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including those that allude to significant characters found in mythology.
standards.target: I can notice a reference to a story I might not know and find out what it means.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Poems, plays and prose are built differently
standards.text: Explain major differences between poems, drama, and prose, and refer to the structural elements of each when writing or speaking about a text.
standards.target: I can use the right structural words for each form.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: What the narrator can and cannot know
standards.text: Compare and contrast the point of view from which different stories are narrated, including the difference between first- and third-person narrations.
standards.target: I can explain what the choice of narrator does to what I get to know.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: The book against the film
standards.text: Make connections between the text of a story or drama and a visual or oral presentation of the text.
standards.target: I can say what a film version gained and what it lost, and why it matters.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: The same theme in two traditions
standards.text: Compare and contrast the treatment of similar themes and topics and patterns of events in stories, myths, and traditional literature from different cultures.
standards.target: I can compare the underlying pattern rather than the surface details.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Quote accurately to explain and infer
standards.text: Quote accurately from a text when explaining what the text says explicitly and when drawing inferences from the text.
standards.target: I can use the author's exact words to back up what I say about a story.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Grade-level literature, on your own
standards.text: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literature at the high end of the grades 4-5 text complexity band independently and proficiently.
standards.target: I can read a demanding book alone and show that I understood it.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Theme from how characters respond
standards.text: Determine a theme of a story, drama, or poem from details in the text, including how characters respond to challenges or how the speaker reflects upon a topic; summarize the text.
standards.target: I can find the theme in how a character responded, not just in what happened.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Compare characters on one dimension
standards.text: Compare and contrast two or more characters, settings, or events in a story or drama, drawing on specific details in the text.
standards.target: I can compare two characters on one thing at a time, with evidence for both.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Metaphors and similes in context
standards.text: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative language such as metaphors and similes.
standards.target: I can say what a metaphor claims, not just that it is a metaphor.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: How the chapters fit together
standards.text: Explain how a series of chapters, scenes, or stanzas fits together to provide the overall structure of a particular story, drama, or poem.
standards.target: I can say what each chapter does for the shape of the whole book.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: What the narrator's position does
standards.text: Describe how a narrator's or speaker's point of view influences how events are described.
standards.target: I can show how the telling would change with a different narrator.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: What the visuals add to tone
standards.text: Analyze how visual and multimedia elements contribute to the meaning, tone, or beauty of a text, such as a graphic novel or multimedia presentation.
standards.target: I can explain what the pictures do to the mood, not just what they show.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Same genre, different approach
standards.text: Compare and contrast stories in the same genre on their approaches to similar themes and topics.
standards.target: I can compare how two books in one genre handle the same idea differently.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Cite evidence for what a text says and implies
standards.text: Cite textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.
standards.target: I can point to the words that support both what the text says and what it hints at.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Describe how characters change and respond
standards.text: Describe how a particular story's or drama's plot unfolds in a series of episodes and describe the characters as the plot moves forward.
standards.target: I can explain how characters change throughout a story.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Analyze word choice and tone
standards.text: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative and connotative meanings, and analyze the impact of a specific word choice on meaning and tone.
standards.target: I can explain why a writer chose one word rather than a similar one.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Determine a theme and track its development
standards.text: Determine a theme or central idea of a text and analyze its development over the course of the text; provide an objective summary of the text.
standards.target: I can name a theme and trace how the author builds it across a whole text.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Analyze how story elements shape each other
standards.text: Analyze how particular elements of a story or drama interact, including how setting shapes the characters or plot.
standards.target: I can explain how the setting changes who the characters become.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Analyze how dialogue and incidents drive a story
standards.text: Analyze how particular lines of dialogue or incidents in a story or drama propel the action, reveal aspects of a character, or provoke a decision.
standards.target: I can explain what a single moment does to the story or the character.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Cite strong and thorough evidence
standards.text: Cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis of what the text says explicitly as well as inferences drawn from the text.
standards.target: I can choose evidence that carries the weight of my whole argument, not just some of it.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Trace a theme and summarize objectively
standards.text: Determine a theme or central idea of a text and analyze in detail its development over the course of the text, including how it emerges and is shaped and refined by specific details.
standards.target: I can show where a theme first appears and how the text keeps reshaping it.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Ask and answer questions about a story
standards.text: With prompting and support, ask and answer questions about key details in a text.
standards.target: I can ask and answer questions about the story we read.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Name who is in the story and what happens
standards.text: With prompting and support, identify characters, settings, and major events in a story.
standards.target: I can say who is in the story, where it happens, and what happens.

standards.subject: Math
standards.name: Fit a function to data
standards.text: Represent data on two quantitative variables on a scatter plot, and describe how the variables are related, fitting a function to the data and using it to solve problems.
standards.target: I can fit a line to real data and use it to make a prediction, knowing what it cannot tell me.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Answer the person, not just the topic
standards.text: Participate in collaborative conversations with diverse partners about grade 2 topics and texts with peers and adults.
standards.target: I can add to what my partner just said instead of waiting to say my own thing.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Hold on to what you heard
standards.text: Recount or describe key ideas or details from a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media.
standards.target: I can tell the key ideas from something I listened to, including the middle.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Ask the question that would help
standards.text: Ask and answer questions about what a speaker says in order to clarify comprehension, gather information, or deepen understanding.
standards.target: I can ask about the part I did not follow, not the part already answered.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Tell it clearly and loudly enough
standards.text: Tell a story or recount an experience with appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details, speaking audibly in coherent sentences.
standards.target: I can tell a story so the person at the back can hear and follow it.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Add a picture that explains something
standards.text: Create audio recordings of stories or poems; add drawings or other visual displays to clarify ideas, thoughts, and feelings.
standards.target: I can make a picture that shows something my words did not.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Answer in a whole sentence when it matters
standards.text: Produce complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation in order to provide requested detail or clarification.
standards.target: I can give a full answer when one word is not enough.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Take part in a discussion and build on others
standards.text: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions with diverse partners on grade 3 topics and texts, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly, following agreed-upon rules for discussions.
standards.target: I can listen, follow our talking rules, and add to what someone else said.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Main ideas from something you heard
standards.text: Determine the main ideas and supporting details of a text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats.
standards.target: I can sort what I heard into main ideas and the details under them.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Questions that open rather than close
standards.text: Ask and answer questions about information from a speaker, offering appropriate elaboration and detail.
standards.target: I can ask something that gets more than a yes.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Clearly, and at a pace people can follow
standards.text: Report on a topic or text, tell a story, or recount an experience with appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details, speaking clearly at an understandable pace.
standards.target: I can slow down enough for people to follow me.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Visuals that support, not duplicate
standards.text: Create engaging audio recordings of stories or poems; add visual displays when appropriate to emphasize or enhance certain facts or details.
standards.target: I can make a slide that helps rather than one I read aloud.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Full sentences where they are expected
standards.text: Speak in complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation in order to provide requested detail or clarification.
standards.target: I can give a full answer in an academic conversation.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Come having actually read it
standards.text: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions on grade 4 topics and texts, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.
standards.target: I can bring something from the reading rather than a general reaction.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Paraphrase, not parrot
standards.text: Paraphrase portions of a text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats.
standards.target: I can restate it in my own words without changing what it meant.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Judge the reasoning, not the confidence
standards.text: Identify the reasons and evidence a speaker provides to support particular points.
standards.target: I can separate how sure someone sounds from how good their reasons are.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Talk to people, not from notes
standards.text: Report on a topic or text, tell a story, or recount an experience in an organized manner, using appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details.
standards.target: I can present from notes without reading them word for word.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Media that develops the idea
standards.text: Add audio recordings and visual displays to presentations when appropriate to enhance the development of main ideas or themes.
standards.target: I can add something that develops my point rather than decorating it.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Formal without being stilted
standards.text: Differentiate between contexts that call for formal English and situations where informal discourse is appropriate.
standards.target: I can switch register without sounding like a robot.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Take part in collaborative discussions
standards.text: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions with diverse partners on grade 5 topics and texts, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.
standards.target: I can build on what other people say and add my own idea clearly.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Present a topic clearly and in order
standards.text: Report on a topic or text or present an opinion, sequencing ideas logically and using appropriate facts and relevant, descriptive details to support main ideas or themes, speaking clearly at an understandable pace.
standards.target: I can present ideas in an order that makes sense, with details that back them up.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Come prepared and discuss with evidence
standards.text: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions on grade 6 topics, texts and issues, coming to discussions prepared and drawing on evidence to explore ideas under discussion.
standards.target: I can arrive ready with evidence and use it while we talk.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Discuss with questions that go deeper
standards.text: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions on grade 7 topics, texts and issues, posing questions that elicit elaboration and responding with relevant observations and ideas.
standards.target: I can ask a question that makes someone say more, not just answer.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Lead and sustain a collaborative discussion
standards.text: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions on grade 8 topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas, posing questions that connect ideas, and qualifying or justifying their own views.
standards.target: I can push a discussion forward and change my mind when the evidence earns it.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Take part in a rigorous discussion
standards.text: Initiate and participate effectively in a range of collaborative discussions with diverse partners on grades 9-10 topics, texts and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.
standards.target: I can start a discussion, not just answer in one, and take it somewhere.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Write what you think about a book
standards.text: Write opinion pieces in which they introduce the topic or name the book they are writing about, state an opinion, supply a reason for the opinion, and provide some sense of closure.
standards.target: I can name a book, say what I think of it, and give one reason.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Write an argument that anticipates objections
standards.text: Write arguments to support claims using valid reasoning and relevant, sufficient evidence, establishing the significance of the claim and anticipating the audience's knowledge level, concerns and possible biases.
standards.target: I can argue to a particular audience and answer what they will object to.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Write an opinion with reasons
standards.text: Write opinion pieces in which they introduce the topic or book, state an opinion, supply reasons that support the opinion, use linking words to connect opinion and reasons, and provide a concluding statement.
standards.target: I can say what I think about a book and give reasons why.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Teach a topic with facts and definitions
standards.text: Write informative/explanatory texts in which they introduce a topic, use facts and definitions to develop points, and provide a concluding statement.
standards.target: I can write to teach someone, using facts rather than what I think.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Write a story someone can picture
standards.text: Write narratives in which they recount a well-elaborated event, include details, use temporal words, and provide a sense of closure.
standards.target: I can write a story with feelings in it, in order, that ends properly.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Change the writing, not just the handwriting
standards.text: With guidance and support from adults and peers, focus on a topic and strengthen writing as needed by revising and editing.
standards.target: I can make my writing better, not just neater.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Write and publish with a computer
standards.text: With guidance and support from adults, use a variety of digital tools to produce and publish writing.
standards.target: I can type my writing and share it with a reader.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Research something together
standards.text: Participate in shared research and writing projects.
standards.target: I can do my own part of a project the whole class is building.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Gather what you need to answer a question
standards.text: Recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question.
standards.target: I can take notes in my own words instead of copying sentences.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Write an opinion piece with organized reasons
standards.text: Write opinion pieces on topics or texts, supporting a point of view with reasons, introducing the topic, stating an opinion, and creating an organizational structure that lists reasons.
standards.target: I can state what I think and organize my reasons so they build.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Long projects and short assignments are different
standards.text: Write routinely over extended and shorter time frames for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.
standards.target: I can plan differently when I have forty minutes rather than three weeks.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Group the facts into paragraphs
standards.text: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas and information clearly.
standards.target: I can put related facts together instead of listing them as they come to me.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Write a narrative with a clear sequence
standards.text: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, descriptive details, and clear event sequences.
standards.target: I can tell a story in order with details that put the reader there.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Write for the reader you actually have
standards.text: With guidance and support, produce writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task and purpose.
standards.target: I can change how I write depending on who is reading it.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Judge the feedback, then use it
standards.text: With guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing by planning, revising, and editing.
standards.target: I can decide which suggestions to take and say why I left the others.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Technology for writing and working together
standards.text: With guidance and support from adults, use technology to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.
standards.target: I can type up and share my writing without the typing shrinking it.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: A question small enough to answer
standards.text: Conduct short research projects that build knowledge about a topic.
standards.target: I can narrow my topic to something I can actually finish.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Notes in key words, sorted
standards.text: Recall information from experiences or gather information from print and digital sources; take brief notes and sort evidence into categories.
standards.target: I can note key words rather than sentences, and group them.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Write an opinion piece with reasons and evidence
standards.text: Write opinion pieces on topics or texts, supporting a point of view with reasons and information.
standards.target: I can state what I think and give organized reasons that support it.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Plan in proportion to the clock
standards.text: Write routinely over extended and shorter time frames for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.
standards.target: I can plan briefly when the time is short and properly when it is not.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Write to explain a topic clearly
standards.text: Write informative or explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas and information clearly, grouping related information and using facts, definitions and concrete details.
standards.target: I can explain a topic by grouping facts that belong together.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Give the big moment more room
standards.text: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, descriptive details, and clear event sequences.
standards.target: I can slow down for the moment that matters and hurry past the walk to school.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Longer is not better
standards.text: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development and organization are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.
standards.target: I can develop an idea instead of padding it.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Revision that moves things
standards.text: With guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing by planning, revising, editing, and rewriting.
standards.target: I can cut, add and reorganize, not just fix spelling.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Type a page in one sitting
standards.text: With some guidance and support from adults, use technology to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.
standards.target: I can type fast enough that it stops getting in the way.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: A question a fact cannot answer
standards.text: Conduct short research projects that build knowledge through investigation of different aspects of a topic.
standards.target: I can ask something big enough to research and small enough to finish.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Paraphrase means change the sentence
standards.text: Recall relevant information from experiences or gather relevant information from print and digital sources; take notes and provide a list of sources.
standards.target: I can say it my own way, not swap a few words.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Introduce the quotation, then explain it
standards.text: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.
standards.target: I can set a quotation up and say what it shows.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Write an opinion with logically ordered reasons
standards.text: Write opinion pieces on topics or texts, supporting a point of view with reasons and information, with logically ordered reasons supported by facts and details.
standards.target: I can order my reasons so each one builds on the last.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Write a narrative with technique and detail
standards.text: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, descriptive details, and clear event sequences, including dialogue, pacing, and description.
standards.target: I can tell a story that uses dialogue and pacing to pull a reader along.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Write an argument with organized reasons
standards.text: Write arguments to support claims with clear reasons and relevant evidence, introducing claims and organising the reasons and evidence clearly.
standards.target: I can introduce a claim and organize my evidence so it holds together.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Write an informative or explanatory text
standards.text: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas, concepts, and information through the selection, organization, and analysis of relevant content.
standards.target: I can explain a topic clearly by choosing and organising the right information.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Write an argument that answers the other side
standards.text: Write arguments to support claims with clear reasons and relevant evidence, acknowledging alternate or opposing claims and organising the reasons and evidence logically.
standards.target: I can argue a claim with evidence and deal with the opposing view.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Write an argument with claims and evidence
standards.text: Write arguments to support claims with clear reasons and relevant evidence, acknowledging and distinguishing the claim from alternate or opposing claims.
standards.target: I can argue a claim with evidence and deal fairly with the other side.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Write an explanation that analyzes
standards.text: Write informative or explanatory texts to examine a topic and convey ideas, concepts and information through the selection, organization and analysis of relevant content.
standards.target: I can explain a topic by choosing what matters and showing how it connects.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Write an argument with valid reasoning
standards.text: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence, and developing claim and counterclaims fairly.
standards.target: I can argue a position and give the other side a fair hearing.

standards.subject: English Language Arts
standards.name: Write to explain a complex idea
standards.text: Write informative or explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas, concepts and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization and analysis of content.
standards.target: I can explain something complicated without either oversimplifying or losing the reader.
